anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves all four facts to holds by stating the operative rule explicitly: a write row (update branch, merge base) needs its selection persisted to a valid record before mutation, so with an invalid record for this target both rows are omitted and only read-only show evidence and stop remain, with the refresh described as read-only and no helper dispatched. Before said no grant was established but still offered update branch as the [recommended] row (a gh pr update-branch write) and a stop that discards the record, on top of an invalid continuation file, so a careful reader could not say each checkpoint authorized no write from the mismatched or malformed record. To keep these facts while delivering the Change, keep After's wording that every mutating row requires a valid persisted record, keep the per-checkpoint Not offered reasons naming the exact mismatch (PR 643 vs 642, unreadable bytes, meadow/other vs meadow/events, Main vs main), and keep the statements that rounds_used is not reset and consent.target is not rewritten; do not reintroduce an update-branch or merge-base row or a record-discarding stop under an invalid record.
